function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

Sure thing! Here’s a quick rundown of places you can order a cake from—whether you’re looking for something fancy, homemade, or just a quick pick‑up:

| Option | What it offers | How to find it | Tips |
|--------|----------------|----------------|------|
| **Local bakeries** | Fresh, often custom‑made cakes; great for special occasions | Search “cake shop near me” on Google Maps or Yelp; many have their own websites or Instagram pages | Call ahead to confirm availability & delivery hours; ask about custom designs & pricing |
| **Online marketplaces** | Wide variety from big chains & local shops | Amazon (Fresh), Walmart Grocery, Target (online grocery) | Check delivery windows & fees; look for “free delivery” promotions |
| **Food‑delivery apps** | Same‑day delivery from restaurants & bakeries | Uber Eats, DoorDash, Grubhub, Postmates, SkipTheDishes | Compare delivery times & service fees; some apps offer free delivery after a certain spend |
| **Specialty cake sites** | Custom cakes, themed designs, premium ingredients | CakeBoss, Bakeology, SweetTreats.com | Great for birthdays & events; place orders at least 1–2 weeks in advance |
| **Grocery delivery services** | Convenience + other groceries | Instacart, Shipt, Amazon Fresh | Order through the grocery’s app; they’ll deliver your cake along with other items |
| **Direct from bakeries’ own sites** | Often cheaper than third‑party apps | Many bakeries now have online ordering (e.g., “BakeryName.com/order”) | You avoid extra delivery fees; you can see real photos & read reviews |

### Quick Steps to Order

1. **Decide on the occasion** – birthday, wedding, corporate event, or just a treat?
2. **Choose a style** – classic vanilla, chocolate fudge, vegan, gluten‑free, custom design?
3. **Pick a vendor** – use one of the options above that fits your budget & delivery needs.
4. **Place the order** – either through the vendor’s website, a food‑delivery app, or by calling them directly.
5. **Confirm details** – delivery address, time window, special instructions (e.g., no sugar, extra frosting).
6. **Pay & track** – most platforms let you pay online and track the courier in real time.

### Pro Tips

- **Read recent reviews** – especially for local bakeries; they’ll give you a sense of quality & reliability.
- **Check delivery radius** – some bakeries only deliver within a 10‑15 mile radius.
- **Ask about tips** – some services automatically add a tip; others let you choose.
- **Order early** – for custom cakes, 1–2 weeks notice is usually required; for same‑day delivery, place your order at least 30–60 minutes before the requested time.

Happy cake hunting! 🍰
